resources.string: Connect to your computer or server over SSH and use the dsh installed there (0.2.2 or later): conversations, trajectories and approvals stay on the phone, while commands and file work happen on the computer. The computer needs a running sshd and must be able to run dsh (Linux / macOS).

Remote conversations have no phone capabilities (screen, notifications, SMS, file attachments…) and no session modes; the model comes from the computer\'s dsh, and images are sent along with messages. After a network drop or switch the app reconnects and continues the task.
Runs on the phone and can operate it
Ends dsh on the computer; the next message reconnects
IPv4, IPv6 or a domain name, e.g. 192.168.1.10, home.example.com
Paste an OpenSSH or PEM private key (ed25519, ECDSA, RSA), or import a file
Leave empty if the key is not encrypted
New conversations start here; empty = the home directory, ~/ works
If it is not found, enter the full path (run which dsh on the computer), or e.g. npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh
A provider and model id the computer\'s dsh can use, e.g. deepseek-official / deepseek-flash
Use this phone\'s DeepSeek API key
Handed to the computer\'s dsh over the SSH channel (never written to its disk or shown in its command line); off = the computer\'s own configuration
One KEY=value per line, passed to dsh on the computer
Checked on every connection; a change is reported loudly and refused
The first Test connection shows the computer\'s SHA256 fingerprint; nothing connects until you confirm it
Paste or import a private key
Environment variables must be one KEY=value per line
First connection: confirm the host key
The host key fingerprint of %1$s is:
Check it on the computer with ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub and trust it only if it matches; every later connection is checked against it.

The host key of %1$s is not the one you trusted.

Before: %2$s
Now: %3$s

Someone may be impersonating this computer (a man-in-the-middle attack) and could capture your password and conversations. Trust the new key only if you know the computer was reinstalled or its SSH host keys were regenerated, and you checked the new fingerprint on the computer.
I checked the new fingerprint on the computer
Deletes its connection details, the saved password / key, and its conversations on this phone. dsh\'s own sessions on the computer are not touched.
The connection to the computer dropped; reconnecting and continuing the task…
The connection to the computer dropped; this turn was interrupted.
The phone has no network connection.
Cannot resolve the host name: check the domain, or use an IP address.
Connection timed out: the computer is offline, the address is wrong, or the networks cannot reach each other (outside your LAN you need a public address, port forwarding or e.g. Tailscale).
Connection refused: sshd is not running on the computer, or the port is wrong.
Network unreachable: there is no route between the phone and the computer.
This computer\'s host key is not confirmed yet: open it in Settings → Remote hosts, tap Test connection and check the fingerprint.

⚠ The computer\'s host key changed (now %1$s), so the connection was refused: someone may be impersonating it. If you reinstalled it or changed its keys, check and trust the new key in Settings → Remote hosts.
Authentication failed: wrong user name or password, or the computer does not accept this key (check ~/.ssh/authorized_keys).
Cannot read the private key (%1$s): OpenSSH and PEM formats are supported.
Wrong key passphrase, or the key is encrypted and no passphrase was entered.
Cannot enter the working directory on the computer: %1$s
dsh was not found on the computer (%1$s). Install it there (npm i -g @deepseek-ai/dsh), or enter the full path of the dsh command in the host settings.
dsh failed to start on the computer: %1$s
The computer\'s dsh refused the model: %1$s. Check the model in the host settings, or the providers configured in dsh on the computer.
